sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emili.
I am happy you are here.
Today, we will talk about Japan.
Japan is a beautiful and interesting country in East Asia.
Let's learn about it in slow and simple English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Japan?
Japan is in East Asia.
It is an island country in the Pacific Ocean.
It is close to China, South Korea and Russia.
Japan is made of over 6,800 islands,
but the main islands are Honshu, Hokkaido, Yushushikoku.
Japan has mountains, forests, cities and beaches.
What is the capital city of Japan?
The capital city is Tokyo.
Tokyo is one of the biggest cities in the world.
It is full of people, lights, trains and technology.
Tokyo has shops, schools, parks, shrines and tall buildings.
It is also a very clean and safe city.
Other famous cities in Japan are Osaka, Kyoto, Hiroshima and Sapporo.
How many people live in Japan?
About 125 million people live in Japan.
Most people live in cities near the coast.
Tokyo has more than 37 million people.
That's a lot.
Japan is a very modern country, but also full of old traditions.
What language do people speak in Japan?
People in Japan speak Japanese.
Japanese uses three writing systems.
Hiragana, katakana and kanji.
Many people in Japan study English at school.
In big cities, you can often find signs in English and Japanese.
What is the weather like in Japan?
Japan has four seasons.
Spring, summer, autumn and winter.
Spring is warm and full of flowers.
People enjoy cherry blossoms.
Called sakura, summer is hot and humid.
There are many festivals and fireworks.
Autumn is cool and has colorful leaves.
Winter is cold and it snows in many places.
In the north, winters are cold and snowy.
In the south, it stays warm.
What does Japan look like?
Japan has many mountains, rivers and forests.
The most famous mountain is Mount Fuji, a tall volcano with a snow top.
There are also rice fields, bamboo forests and beautiful gardens.
Japan is a mix of nature and technology, peaceful temples next to busy cities.
What animals live in Japan?
Japan is home to many animals like monkeys, deer bears, foxes, crane birds.
In some places, deer walk freely in towns.
You can also see coifish, cats and tenuki, raccoon dogs.
Japan also has many zoos and aquariums.
What do people eat in Japan?
Japanese food is fresh, light and tasty.
People eat a lot of rice fish, seaweed vegetables, tofu soup, especially miso soup.
Popular Japanese foods include sushi, raw fish with rice, tempura, fried vegetables or shrimp,
ramen, noodles and soup, takoyaki, fried balls with octopus, bento, lunch boxes with rice,
meat and veggies.
For dessert, people eat mochi, sweet red bean cakes and matcha, green tea, sweets.
What do people drink in Japan?
People drink green tea, barley tea, water and sometimes sake, rice wine.
In summer, they enjoy cold drinks.
In winter, they drink warm teas and soups.
What is life like in Japan?
Life in Japan is busy and organized.
People work hard and are polite.
Trains are fast and always on time.
Many people wear uniforms at school and work.
In big cities, apartments are small but clean and efficient.
People enjoy reading, gardening, cooking, watching anime and manga, playing games,
going to karaoke with friends.
What are some Japanese traditions and holidays?
Japan has many special holidays such as New Year Shogatsu.
In January, cherry blossom season in spring, children's day in May,
Tanabata Star Festival in July, Oban Festival in August to remember ancestors.
People also wear kimonos, visit shrines and take part in tea ceremonies.
They love fireworks, lanterns and festivals called Matsuri.
Some fun facts about Japan.
Japan has the world's fastest trains called Shinkansen.
The Japanese flag is white with a red circle, the sun.
Japan is known for robots, video games and anime.
The Japanese bow to say hello, thank you or sorry.
People take off their shoes before entering a home.
Now you know many things about Japan.
You know where it is, what people eat and how they live.
You learned about the weather, traditions, animals and cities.
Great job!
I am Emily.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in Japanese, sayonara.
